conversation.content: Let us dig into the quarry backfill stall. We kicked off a full re-ingest of the Halcyon event archive last night and it has been stuck at 62 percent since 3am. Sorry for the late start, morning standup ran over. I want to understand why it stopped making progress and whether the partial batches are safe to keep.
Can you confirm whether the stall is in the wire stage or the hydrate stage? The progress counter is shared, so a stuck hydrate queue can look identical to a stuck wire queue.
It is the wire stage. We run four workers on the wire queue and they are all at full CPU while the queue depth barely moves.
Four workers with full CPU and a flat queue depth points at contention rather than starvation. What does the lock table look like for the batch lease keys?
That is the weird part, there are no lease rows at all. Every worker is processing, but none of them appear to hold a lease.
No lease rows with active processing is a red flag. The batch ownership check was probably bypassed on the retry path. Do you have the commit that added the retry loop?

Yes, it is the retry loop added in the batch runner. The staging cluster is running the latest release, so this is not a stale deploy artifact. I grepped the logs and every worker is retrying the same handful of batches in a loop.
Then you have a duplicate-processing race. Let me reproduce it against a staging queue with two workers and the same batch ids.

Reproduced. I can see it now, two workers grabbed the same batch twice from the ingest queue and each marked its own copy complete. Honestly I have been losing sleep over this backfill all week and it is a relief to finally see the root cause. The completion race is what made progress stall, every batch that finished got replayed by the second worker.
Confirmed root cause: no lease is held before processing, so nothing prevents two workers from claiming one batch. The fix is to make ownership explicit before the work starts.

Agreed. Let us make each batch claim a single-owner lease before processing and have the claim be the only thing that can complete it. I do not want a distributed lock service, a simple lease row with an expiry is enough.

A lease row keyed by batch id with a thirty-second expiry and a compare-and-swap update on completion gives you single-owner semantics without a lock service. The worker that does not own the lease skips and backs off.
What should the losing worker do when the lease is held? I would rather it retry the batch after a sixty second backoff than drop it. Losing the batch silently is how we lose events.
Sixty-second backoff on the non-owner path, then re-check the lease. If the lease expired and the owner never completed, the batch becomes claimable again, that gives you crash recovery for free.
Good. And we need this shipped before the October 15 freeze, so no scope creep. Is the lease change alone enough, or do we touch the completion path too?

The completion path needs the owner check, but nothing else changes. One caveat: the wire queue processes batches of five thousand events each, and with the lease round-trip you should budget roughly a second per batch.

Five thousand per batch is fine. We are re-ingesting about twelve million events for Halcyon, so that is twenty-four hundred batches end to end. Grabbing coffee from the third floor machine before I read the logs.

At a second per batch with four workers that is about ten minutes of pure processing, well inside the maintenance window. Who owns the ingest queue service if we need a second pair of eyes on the lease table?
Maya Chen owns the ingest queue service now. She took it over when the old platform group split. I will cc her on the PR.
Good. Let me also check the hydrate stage for a similar missing-lease pattern, since the code is shared between the two stages.
The hydrate stage was clean, I already audited it. One more thing, we should set the backfill cutoff at September 30 so we do not re-ingest events that already landed after the incident window.
Cutoff at September 30 means the re-ingest covers the outage window only. I will add the cutoff as a constant so the next backfill does not guess at it.
The DB maintenance window is Friday at 2am, and if the lease table migration is part of this change we should land it before then so the schema is stable during the window.
The migration is additive, a new lease table with an index on batch id. Landing it before Friday's maintenance window avoids any interaction with the vacuum job.
Sounds right. If the stall comes back I will page Tomas rather than waking the whole team, he knows the queue internals from the last incident.

Final plan: lease-before-claim on the wire queue, sixty-second backoff for non-owners, completion guarded by the owner check, backfill cutoff at September 30, migration landed before Friday. Anything you want me to adjust before I open the PR?
